note: Every number this app shows about diet, activity, sleep, hydration or risk thresholds traces to one of these sources. Nothing here is invented. Where a source gives a range, the app shows the range.

dga2025.title: Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2025–2030
dga2025.publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services & U.S. Department of Agriculture
usedFor: Protein target of 1.2–1.6 g per kg of body weight per day
Dairy: 3 servings/day at a 2,000-calorie pattern
Vegetables: 3 servings/day; Fruits: 2 servings/day at a 2,000-calorie pattern
Whole grains: 2–4 servings/day
Saturated fat: under 10% of total daily calories
Added sugars: no amount recommended; no more than 10 g in any one meal
Sodium: under 2,300 mg/day for ages 14+
Choose water (still or sparkling) and unsweetened beverages; avoid sugar-sweetened drinks
Prioritise minimally processed whole foods; avoid ultra-processed foods, artificial dyes and non-nutritive sweeteners
Fermented foods and high-fibre foods support a diverse gut microbiome

dgaServings.title: Daily Servings by Calorie Level (Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2025–2030)
usedFor: Food-group serving counts for the 1,800 and 2,000 calorie patterns

Serving-size definitions: 3 oz cooked meat/poultry/seafood, 1 egg, ½ cup beans/peas/lentils, 1 oz nuts or seeds, 2 tbsp nut butter, 3 oz soy = 1 protein serving; 1 cup milk, ¾ cup yogurt, 1 oz cheese = 1 dairy serving; 1 cup raw or cooked vegetables or 2 cups leafy greens = 1 vegetable serving; 1 cup raw fruit or ½ cup dried = 1 fruit serving; ½ cup cooked grain, 1 slice bread or 1 tortilla = 1 whole-grain serving; 1 tsp olive oil or butter = 1 healthy-fat serving

fdc.title: FoodData Central — SR Legacy (April 2018 release)
usedFor: Every calorie, protein, fat, saturated fat, carbohydrate, fibre, sugar, sodium, potassium, calcium, iron, magnesium and caffeine figure in this app
Household portion weights (cup, slice, tortilla, tsp) used to convert servings to grams
fdc.note: Each food in data/foods.json carries its USDA FDC ID and the exact USDA description, so any number can be checked at fdc.nal.usda.gov.

pag2.title: Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd edition
pag2.publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
usedFor: 150–300 minutes/week of moderate-intensity aerobic activity, or 75–150 minutes vigorous, or an equivalent mix
Muscle-strengthening activity on 2 or more days per week working all major muscle groups
Activity can be accumulated in short bouts across the day

cdcAdultPA.title: Adult Activity: An Overview
cdcAdultPA.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
usedFor: Plain-language restatement of the weekly aerobic and strength targets

acsm2026.title: Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy and Performance — ACSM Position Stand (2026 update)
usedFor: Train all major muscle groups at least twice per week
Strength emphasis: heavier loads around 80% of 1RM for 2–3 sets per exercise
Hypertrophy emphasis: about 10 sets per muscle group per week
Bodyweight, bands and home-based routines produce marked gains in strength, size and function — a gym is not required
Training to failure and complex periodisation are not required for the average healthy adult

ahaCrf.title: Importance of Assessing Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Clinical Practice: A Case for Fitness as a Clinical Vital Sign (Scientific Statement)
usedFor: Cardiorespiratory fitness is a stronger predictor of mortality than smoking, hypertension, high cholesterol or type 2 diabetes
Low fitness in men is an estimated peak VO2 below 28 mL/kg/min
Fitness should be estimated at least yearly

le8.title: Life's Essential 8: Updating and Enhancing the American Heart Association's Construct of Cardiovascular Health (Presidential Advisory)
usedFor: The eight components this app tracks for long-term health: diet, physical activity, nicotine exposure, sleep, body mass index, blood lipids (non-HDL cholesterol), blood glucose and blood pressure
le8.note: This app tracks the eight components against each one's own published target. It does not reproduce AHA's 0–100 point scoring algorithm.

aasmSleep.title: Seven or more hours of sleep per night: a health necessity for adults (AASM/SRS consensus)
aasmSleep.publisher: American Academy of Sleep Medicine & Sleep Research Society
usedFor: Adults should sleep 7 or more hours per night
Six or fewer hours per night is inadequate to sustain health

cdcSleep.title: About Sleep / How to Improve Your Sleep
cdcSleep.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
usedFor: Keep the same bed and wake times, including weekends
Avoid caffeine for 5 or more hours before bed — more if you are sensitive
Avoid large meals and alcohol before bed; keep the bedroom dark and quiet

nasemWater.title: Dietary Reference Intakes for Water, Potassium, Sodium, Chloride, and Sulfate
nasemWater.publisher: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (2005)
usedFor: Adequate Intake of total water for men 19–30: 3.7 L/day, of which about 3.0 L (13 cups) comes from drinks
Thirst is an adequate guide for most healthy people; needs rise with heat and heavy activity

nasemFiber.title: Dietary Reference Intakes for Energy, Carbohydrate, Fiber, Fat, Fatty Acids, Cholesterol, Protein, and Amino Acids
nasemFiber.publisher: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (2005)
usedFor: Adequate Intake for total fibre: 38 g/day for men aged 19–50

cdcBmi.title: Adult BMI Categories
cdcBmi.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
usedFor: BMI categories: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5–24.9 healthy weight, 25.0–29.9 overweight, 30.0+ obesity
BMI is a screening measure and should be read alongside other measures

cdcWeightLoss.title: Steps for Losing Weight
cdcWeightLoss.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
usedFor: A gradual pace of about 1 to 2 pounds per week is more likely to stay off
Healthy weight loss combines eating pattern, activity, sleep and stress management

cdcBp.title: About High Blood Pressure
cdcBp.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
usedFor: Normal blood pressure: systolic under 120 and diastolic under 80 mm Hg
Elevated: systolic 120–129 with diastolic under 80
High blood pressure: systolic 130 or higher, or diastolic 80 or higher

cdcCholesterol.title: Cholesterol: What Your Numbers Mean (consumer education sheet)
cdcCholesterol.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
usedFor: Desirable total cholesterol: under 200 mg/dL
Desirable LDL cholesterol: under 100 mg/dL
Desirable HDL cholesterol: 40 mg/dL or above
Desirable triglycerides: under 150 mg/dL

cdcA1c.title: A1C Test for Diabetes and Prediabetes
cdcA1c.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
usedFor: A1c under 5.7% is normal; 5.7–6.4% is prediabetes; 6.5% or above indicates diabetes
Fasting plasma glucose 100–125 mg/dL indicates prediabetes

nhlbiWeight.title: Heart-Healthy Living — Aim for a Healthy Weight
nhlbiWeight.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, NIH
usedFor: A waist circumference over 40 inches raises risk of heart disease and type 2 diabetes in men
For adults with overweight or obesity, aim to lose 5–10% of starting weight over about six months

uspstfDiabetes.title: Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes: Screening
usedFor: Screen adults aged 35–70 who have overweight (BMI 25+) or obesity (BMI 30+) for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes

uspstfHtn.title: Hypertension in Adults: Screening
usedFor: Screen adults aged 18 and over for high blood pressure

mayoIf.title: Intermittent fasting: What are the benefits?
usedFor: Short-term trials show weight loss and metabolic improvement; longer trials (6–12 months) are mixed
Possible side effects: fatigue, dizziness, headaches, mood changes
People with diabetes, on medication, or with a history of eating disorders should not start without medical advice

hopkinsIf.title: Intermittent Fasting: What Is It, and How Does It Work?
usedFor: Time-restricted eating (for example, an 8-hour daily eating window) is the most common form of intermittent fasting
Reported effects include weight loss and improved insulin sensitivity

nihTre.title: Time-restricted eating for metabolic syndrome
nihTre.publisher: National Institutes of Health — NIH Research Matters
usedFor: Clinical-trial evidence on time-restricted eating and metabolic markers

fdaCaffeine.title: Spilling the Beans: How Much Caffeine is Too Much?
usedFor: 400 mg of caffeine per day is not generally associated with negative effects in most healthy adults

nccihGreenTea.title: Green Tea: Usefulness and Safety
nccihGreenTea.publisher: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health, NIH
usedFor: No safety concerns reported for green tea drunk as a beverage by adults
Catechins and caffeine may have a modest effect on body weight; small reductions in total and LDL cholesterol
Benefits are modest and evidence is mixed — tea is not a treatment

nccihTea.title: Tea
nccihTea.publisher: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health, NIH
usedFor: General safety framing for teas and herbal infusions
